opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Black (employee ID E008) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E008.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Full-time Payroll Specialist requested admin to Source Code. Admin is only available to the role that owns the system (Engineer), so the maximum for this employee is write. Recommending write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E008 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read without advanced training; admin is never allowed. Requested admin to Source Code exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Karen Black (E008) requested admin to Source Code. Admin is never permitted for this employee: Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and Karen is a Payroll Specialist, so admin is not allowed even for full-timers. The notes conflict on employment type (HR says full-time, Security DB says contractor with basic training). Under the most restrictive applicable reading (contractor with basic training), the maximum is read; under full-time it would be write. Since admin exceeds both caps and the facts are conflicting/uncertain, I grant the safest applicable maximum: read.

2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.
